Some of the studies can't fully separate the smack from everything else around it. A parent who smacks may differ from one who doesn't in ways the studies struggle to measure, such as how much time they have, or how hard they tend to lose their temper.

What would change my view is better evidence, and the studies that compare children raised apart with children raised together, which try to separate a family's way of life from the smack itself, are worth watching. I'd also want to know what your mother does the rest of the time. As for your partner, they're right that it's your child and your house. They're less sure of themselves than they sound.

The road is worth one thing, since it's the reason for the smack. A four-year-old near a road needs a hand held, a gate and a lot of saying it again. Those work better than the smack, and you can start tonight.
